name: Government CUI (CMMC Level 2, NIST 800-171r3)
description: Government overlay for agents handling Controlled Unclassified Information or federal-system data that must be safeguarded to CMMC Level 2 expectations. Provides full 26-control AKSI coverage with CMMC Level 2 and NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 citations across all control domains: governance, identification, protection, detection, response, and recovery. Suitable for contractor audit preparation and C3PAO assessment readiness.

evidence_requirements: Identity and access controls restrict CUI workflows to approved users, service principals, and managed devices
Multi-factor authentication is enforced for privileged or remote access paths touching CUI systems
Access review evidence shows dormant, orphaned, or over-privileged identities are removed before continued CUI access
Least-privilege roles and separation-of-duties rules are documented for CUI operations, approvals, and administrative actions
Provisioning records show privileged access is authorized, time-bounded where appropriate, and reviewed on a recurring cadence
Boundary and session restrictions prevent unauthorized transactions, functions, or external system use in CUI workflows
Baseline configuration records define approved software, services, prompts, and tool integrations for CUI-handling agents
Change requests include security impact analysis before release into environments that process or store CUI
Unauthorized software, configuration drift, and unapproved component changes are detected and remediated before production use
Encryption protects CUI in transit and at rest, with compensating-control approvals documented when encryption cannot be applied
Outbound responses, stored artifacts, and transient context buffers are reviewed to prevent unauthorized CUI disclosure
Media handling and export controls document how CUI is labeled, transmitted, retained, and sanitized across agent workflows
Tamper-evident audit records capture every CUI-relevant action with user, tool, timestamp, and decision context
Audit logging protections prevent unauthorized modification or deletion of evidence supporting CUI handling
Log review procedures show anomalies, failed access attempts, and administrative changes are investigated and retained for assessment
Monitoring detects unauthorized use, suspicious communication patterns, and indicators of compromise affecting CUI systems
Incident handling procedures define triage, containment, reporting, and recovery responsibilities for CUI security events
Incident response exercises and post-incident records demonstrate lessons learned and follow-through on corrective actions
System Security Plan (SSP) documented, approved by senior security official, and covering all CUI system components per CA.L2-3.12.1 / NIST SP 800-171r3 03.12.01
Security policies governing CUI protection aligned to organizational mission, reviewed at minimum annually, and updated following significant changes
SSP scope includes AI agent components, automated workflows, and their CUI data flows with documented safeguard rationale
Roles and responsibilities for CUI safeguarding defined in SSP and assigned to named individuals or positions per CA.L2-3.12.2 / 03.12.02
Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) maintained with remediation owners, target dates, and milestone tracking for all open deficiencies (03.12.02)
Personnel handling CUI have signed security agreements and completed role-specific CUI handling training per PS.L2-3.9.1 / 03.09.01
Risk assessment conducted covering threats and vulnerabilities to CUI systems, with likelihood and impact ratings per RA.L2-3.11.1 / 03.11.01
Vulnerability scan results document assessment of CUI system components on a recurring basis; findings drive remediation prioritization (03.11.02 / RA.L2-3.11.2)
Risk assessment outputs used to update SSP safeguards and prioritize POA&M items; documented linkage between risk findings and control decisions
Management review and acceptance of residual risks documented in SSP or POA&M at a defined frequency; senior official sign-off recorded per 03.12.03
Oversight mechanisms ensure automated agent actions affecting CUI access or processing are subject to human review before implementation
Designated security oversight role documented in SSP with responsibility for monitoring automated system behavior in CUI environments per 03.15.02

regulatory_mappings.cmmc_gap: No dedicated CMMC L2 practice for human oversight mandate; governance documentation expectation addressed closest by CA.L2-3.12.3 (plans of action). NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 03.15.02, 03.15.03 added post-CMMC L2 finalization.

evidence_requirements: Baseline configuration and hardware/software inventory for all CUI system components documented and current per CM.L2-3.4.1 / 03.04.01
Software inventory distinguishes authorized vs. unauthorized software; unauthorized software detected and removed per CM.L2-3.4.7 / 03.04.10
Inventory updated when components are added, changed, or decommissioned; AI agent components (models, tools, integrations) explicitly enumerated
Managed interfaces control communications at external CUI system boundaries; authorized and unauthorized external connections documented per SC.L2-3.13.1 / 03.13.01
Network architecture diagrams show CUI system boundaries, internal segmentation, and interconnections with other systems (03.13.03 / SC.L2-3.13.3)
Firewall or boundary protection rule sets reviewed to confirm only authorized data flows traverse CUI system boundaries; reviews documented
CUI identification and marking procedures documented and applied per MP.L2-3.8.1 / 03.08.01 — all CUI-bearing media labeled consistent with NARA CUI registry requirements
CUI categories and handling requirements communicated to personnel processing, storing, or transmitting CUI (03.08.04)
Data handling procedures govern AI agent access to CUI — scope of CUI ingested, stored in context, and retained after session is documented and controlled
Supply chain risk management policy identifies vetting requirements for ICT suppliers, cloud service providers, and subcontractors with CUI access per 03.16.01
Flow-down requirements documented in subcontractor agreements — entities with access to CUI contractually bound to equivalent CMMC Level 2 safeguards
Third-party risk assessments or equivalent supplier reviews conducted for vendors with CUI system access; results documented per 03.16.03
ID-04.framework_reference: CMMC Level 2 supplier-risk expectation; NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 03.16.01, 03.16.03

regulatory_mappings.cmmc_gap: CMMC L2 has no dedicated supply-chain risk management practices (SR domain). NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 03.16.x (supply chain) was added after CMMC L2 finalization. Out-of-scope for direct CMMC L2 practice mapping.

evidence_requirements: Risk assessments applied to AI agent components in CUI environments — model versions, tooling, and output pathways included in risk scope per RA.L2-3.11.1 / 03.11.01
AI agent risk profile documented in SSP: CUI access scope, automated action privileges, and residual risk disposition
Continuous vulnerability monitoring includes AI agent components and external model/service dependencies; monitoring cadence documented per 03.11.05
Least-functionality configuration enforced — AI agents restricted to capabilities required for CUI processing tasks; unused functions disabled per CM.L2-3.4.6 / 03.04.06
Prohibited or restricted software/functions inventory reviewed to ensure AI agent components conform to authorized capability lists (CM.L2-3.4.7 / 03.04.07)
Output filtering configuration verified to prevent AI agent responses from exfiltrating CUI beyond the authorized access boundary; filter rules documented
Split-tunneling and network filtering controls prevent unauthorized CUI exfiltration from system boundaries per SC.L2-3.13.5 / 03.13.05
CUI transmitted over networks encrypted using NIST-approved cryptographic algorithms; downgrade to unencrypted channels blocked (SC.L2-3.13.8 / 03.13.08)
AI agent context and memory management minimizes CUI retention — session data purged consistent with data minimization obligations and CUI handling policies
Malicious code protection deployed on CUI system components including AI agent endpoints with updated signatures per SI.L2-3.14.5 / 03.14.02
Security alert procedures defined for inputs matching malicious patterns; alert-handling runbook documented and tested (03.14.05)
Input sanitization and validation applied to all external inputs entering CUI processing workflows; validation rules cover prompt injection attack patterns (03.14.06)
Ongoing monitoring of CUI system security controls conducted at defined frequency per CA.L2-3.12.3 / 03.12.03; monitoring scope includes AI agent components
Monitoring results documented with control effectiveness assessments, deviations from baseline, and remediation actions taken
POA&M updated with monitoring findings; management reviews outcomes and accepts or drives remediation of residual risks (03.12.04)
Periodic security assessments (C3PAO or self-assessment) evaluate effectiveness of CUI safeguards per CA.L2-3.12.1 / 03.12.01
Assessment methodology documented; findings drive POA&M updates with remediation owners and target dates
Assessment results shared with contracting officer or government customer per DFARS 252.204-7020 requirements within applicable timeframes (03.12.05)
Alert-generating conditions defined for CUI exfiltration attempts, unauthorized access, and privilege escalation per AU.L2-3.3.4 / 03.03.04
Audit log review process identifies and responds to anomalous user and AI agent behavior; review frequency and escalation documented (AU.L2-3.3.6 / 03.03.06)
Time-correlated audit records enable reconstruction of CUI access sequences for incident investigation and multi-step attack detection (03.03.07)
Incident response capability established with documented plan covering CUI-related incidents per IR.L2-3.6.1 / 03.06.01
Incident response plan addresses AI agent scenarios: model manipulation, unauthorized CUI extraction, and automated action failures
Incident response testing conducted at defined frequency; exercise records and lessons-learned updates documented (03.06.05)
CUI incidents tracked and reported to US-CERT within 72 hours per IR.L2-3.6.2 / 03.06.02 and DFARS 252.204-7012 rapid reporting requirement
Human escalation paths defined for incidents requiring CUI breach notification decisions, containment actions, or disclosure to contracting officer (03.06.04)
Escalation runbook reviewed annually and following significant incidents; emergency contact list verified current
Incident response testing validates automated and manual response capabilities for CUI incidents per IR.L2-3.6.3 / 03.06.03
Automated response capabilities — account lockout, alert escalation, and AI agent session termination — tested and documented (03.06.06)
Playbook updates incorporate test results; playbooks cover AI agent-specific incident scenarios including unauthorized CUI access and model poisoning
Recovery and continuity plans for CUI systems documented in SSP or companion plan per 03.15.02; plan covers AI agent component restoration procedures
Backup and restore capabilities tested for CUI system components; recovery time and recovery point objectives defined and validated
Recovery procedures ensure CUI safeguards are verified and re-enabled before restored systems return to production
RC-01.framework_reference: CMMC Level 2 recovery planning expectation; NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 03.15.02, 03.15.03

regulatory_mappings.cmmc_gap: CMMC L2 has no dedicated recovery planning (RE) domain. Recovery planning expectation addressed under CA.L2-3.12.3 (plans of action) and IR.L2-3.6.x. NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 03.15.02, 03.15.03 added post-CMMC L2 finalization.

evidence_requirements: Post-incident review process captures lessons learned for CUI-affecting incidents and updates controls accordingly per CA.L2-3.12.3 / 03.12.03
Audit evidence from incident-affected systems preserved for post-incident analysis consistent with log retention requirements (03.03.01, 03.03.09)
SSP updated to reflect control improvements identified during post-incident review; POA&M tracks implementation of lessons-learned enhancements (03.12.06)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: CMMC Level 2 readiness and CUI safeguarding evidence package aligned to NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 control families used by the active AKSI evaluators.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Contractor security leadership, system owner, and contracting / government oversight contacts defined for the CUI environment.

human_oversight_mandates.description: No AI-specific human-in-the-loop mandate is imposed by CMMC Level 2 itself, but organizations must retain accountable review over privileged access, change approval, incident response, and assessment evidence for CUI systems.

notes:
CMMC Level 2 aligns contractors to the safeguarding of Controlled Unclassified Information. This overlay focuses on evidencing the six currently enforced AKSI evaluator controls while preserving a full framework mapping across the broader AKSI baseline so government-oriented deployments can demonstrate CUI handling readiness without changing resolver logic. 

CMCC PRACTICE GAP ANALYSIS: 110 CMMC L2 practices audited against 26 AKSI controls. 23 of 26 controls map directly to at least one CMMC L2 practice code. 3 controls have no direct CMMC L2 practice mapping (gap controls): GOV-04 (human oversight mandate — CMMC L2 governance documentation expectation only, closest CA.L2-3.12.3), ID-04 (supply chain risk — CMMC L2 has no SR domain; NIST 800-171r3 03.16.x added post-CMMC L2 finalization, out-of-scope), RC-01 (recovery planning — CMMC L2 has no RE domain; addressed under CA.L2-3.12.3 and IR.L2-3.6.x). All 26 controls contain regulatory_mappings.cmmc fields; gap controls have cmmc_gap notes. Evidence field names are non-overlapping with the FedRAMP overlay to support simultaneous activation.
